barriers.what_is_NOT_measured: anything about ordering or visibility. Whether a thread may observe another thread's write without the barrier is exactly what one successful schedule cannot establish, and this harness dispatches a single threadgroup on an idle machine - the schedule most likely to succeed by accident. The omitted-barrier variant is recorded as an ENCODING difference and its results are not read as evidence either way
barriers.what_is_measured: that `threadgroup_barrier` emits `447/6` and omitting it removes exactly that instruction; that each memory flag produces its OWN barrier instruction, so mem_threadgroup | mem_device emits TWO rather than one carrying both; that the three single-flag encodings differ in their bytes; and that `simdgroup_barrier` emits no barrier instruction at all here

means: what an atomic DOES, measured by executing vendor-compiled kernels and reading back both the returned value and the memory. The form is named by decoding the program that ran

operation_table.means: the operation this form performs is selected by a four-bit field, so `10090/12` is NOT determined by the form alone - the same encoding computes eight different functions. It is published as a field-selected family rather than counted as one semantic determination, the way `16873/10 simd.prefix_sum` is
operation_table.what_is_not_known: what the eight unassigned codes do. No Metal intrinsic emits them here, and setting the field directly needs the authored path the safety gate refuses

dev_add.means: the operation is read off MEMORY and the returned value off C. They are independent, and the return is only identified when the operation changed the cell - otherwise old and new are the same word
dev_add.note: one thread per address, so the return is unambiguous and the cell moves once. The operand is the same for every operation in this family, which is what makes their results differ

dev_add_immediate.means: the operation is read off MEMORY and the returned value off C. They are independent, and the return is only identified when the operation changed the cell - otherwise old and new are the same word
dev_add_immediate.note: an immediate operand instead of a register one, which the compiler encodes as a different length of the same opcode

dev_and.means: the operation is read off MEMORY and the returned value off C. They are independent, and the return is only identified when the operation changed the cell - otherwise old and new are the same word
dev_and.note: one thread per address, so the return is unambiguous and the cell moves once. The operand is the same for every operation in this family, which is what makes their results differ

dev_atomic_store.means: an atomic store has no return, so the memory is the only observable. The stored value differs per cell, so a store that wrote the wrong cell is visible rather than absorbed
dev_atomic_store.note: an atomic store returns nothing, so the memory is the whole observable - which is why the dispatch entry point that copies A back is the one this file uses

dev_cmpxchg_match.means: both arms are needed: the matching arm alone cannot tell a compare-and-exchange from an unconditional exchange, and the return is checked against the MEMORY rather than against the expectation
dev_cmpxchg_match.note: the expected value MATCHES the cell, so the swap must happen

dev_cmpxchg_mismatch.means: both arms are needed: the matching arm alone cannot tell a compare-and-exchange from an unconditional exchange, and the return is checked against the MEMORY rather than against the expectation
dev_cmpxchg_mismatch.note: the expected value CANNOT match any cell, so the swap must not happen. Without this arm a probe cannot tell a compare-and-exchange from an unconditional one

dev_contended_add.means: atomic if and only if the cell moved by exactly the thread count AND every thread saw a different value. Either alone is satisfiable without atomicity: a lost update keeps the returns distinct, and a non-returning increment keeps the count right
dev_contended_add.note: every thread increments ONE cell. If the read-modify-write is atomic the returns are a permutation of the consecutive values and the cell moves by exactly the thread count. A single-threaded probe cannot tell that from a lost update or from no read-modify-write at all

dev_exchange.means: the operation is read off MEMORY and the returned value off C. They are independent, and the return is only identified when the operation changed the cell - otherwise old and new are the same word
dev_exchange.note: exchange, whose new value does not depend on the old at all

dev_max.means: the operation is read off MEMORY and the returned value off C. They are independent, and the return is only identified when the operation changed the cell - otherwise old and new are the same word
dev_max.note: one thread per address, so the return is unambiguous and the cell moves once. The operand is the same for every operation in this family, which is what makes their results differ

dev_max_signbit.means: the operation is read off MEMORY and the returned value off C. They are independent, and the return is only identified when the operation changed the cell - otherwise old and new are the same word
dev_max_signbit.note: 0x80000000 is the LARGEST unsigned value and the SMALLEST signed one, so this input separates the two readings of max and nothing else does

tg_add_returning.means: the operation is read off MEMORY and the returned value off C. They are independent, and the return is only identified when the operation changed the cell - otherwise old and new are the same word
tg_add_returning.note: a threadgroup read-modify-write whose value is USED, which the compiler encodes differently from the discarded one. The cell is initialised in threadgroup memory and read back into A, so both observables survive the dispatch

tg_contended_add.means: atomic if and only if the cell moved by exactly the thread count AND every thread saw a different value. Either alone is satisfiable without atomicity: a lost update keeps the returns distinct, and a non-returning increment keeps the count right
tg_contended_add.note: the same contention question in threadgroup memory, which needs a real allocation - without one the array has no storage and every read is zero

what_this_is_not: not a claim about ORDERING. Every probe here uses memory_order_relaxed and a single dispatch, so what is measured is the read-modify-write and its return - not what any thread may observe of another thread's writes, which one successful schedule can never establish
why_this_instrument: g17safe refuses every atomic opcode as MayLoad/MayStore/atomic, so the authored oracle cannot reach them. The gate is about bytes this project wrote pointed at an address nobody checked, not about whether atomics may run
